definition: The large amplitude of a forced oscillation when the driving frequency equals, or is very close to, the natural frequency of the system.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when it is displaced and then left to oscillate freely, with no driving force.
An oscillation caused by an external periodic force; once steady, it has the frequency of the driving force, not the natural frequency.

The loss of energy from an oscillating system through resistive forces such as friction or air resistance, so its amplitude decreases; in a driven system it lowers the resonance peak and shifts it to a slightly lower frequency.
The amount of damping at which a displaced system returns to equilibrium in the shortest possible time without oscillating.
